title: Build a retry queue from a failed run
task: Run bash dispatch.sh. Save its stdout to sent.txt, each exact retry diagnostic line to retry.txt in its original order, and the exit status as a single number in dispatch.status. Keep warnings out of retry.txt.
hints: Run the script once and identify its normal output and diagnostic lines.
Redirect stderr to a temporary file, then match retry lines with a pattern anchored at the start.
Capture the dispatch status before running grep. In a script with errexit, use status=0 and append || status=$? to the dispatch command.

checks.label: The sent report contains only stdout
checks.feedback: Keep the normal output separate from the diagnostics.

checks.label: The retry queue contains only retry lines
checks.feedback: Use an anchored match on stderr. Keep the original order and exclude warnings.

checks.label: The dispatcher’s exit status was preserved
checks.feedback: Record the status immediately after dispatch.sh, before running grep or cat.

demo.command: status=0; bash send-sample.sh > sent.out 2> messages.log || status=$?
demo.visual:
sent.out: sent search
messages.log: retry image
status: 4
demo.explanation: The command saves normal output and diagnostics separately, and preserves the failed dispatch status.
The anchor matches retry at the start and the following space keeps the word match precise.
